summary:
Version 3.3 is frozen. The tag v33-frozen is 0065f1e2 in P/v33/sdkgen (branch freeze), and the tree is clean after `npm run build`. The tools are in P/v33/tools at d3b258d, tagged v33-frozen-tools, also clean.

**Part 1: the shared engineer's work, merged.** I brought over the shared engineer's 5 non-build commits (adbb0944, 862f0e42, 4fde2041, ed05cf2a, 76779043) onto v33a, in order and with no conflicts. Their tools had nothing after 740dc90.

Run against the new facts, the guard first passed only 54 of 77 tests. The failures were mostly cases where the guard read a fact differently from the provider, not runtimes that were wrong:
- the deleted read: the guard took `var` from '{var}.deleted()' as the member name, and could not see c's function-pointer member or zig's struct field;
- facts.arity had no account at all;
- the utility getter's copy had no citations in nine languages, and the match getter's had none in c, clojure and zig;
- swift's record check still assumed the unwrap sits inside the record fact (decision 12 moved it out);
- ocaml still cited a note that decision 9 removed.

I fixed the guard and forms, added citations taken from the runtime lines, declared ts's utility getter `copy: false`, and declared ts's entity name as a field. The guard then passed 77 of 77.

The mutation runs found two more holes in the guard, which I also closed:
- dropping `copy: true` from c's match getter passed the guard, because a citation of an undeclared fact was excused as "ahead of a provider";
- dropping ocaml's field flag passed, because a missing flag was never checked.

**Shared source I changed:**
- direct's Returns paragraph, the two sentences the sentence round's checker called awkward;
- the shared engineer's new list sentence. It said `list(nil, nil)` "lists every record", which brings back an overstatement the sentence round had removed: go's List and ts's list both pass the entity's stored match.
- perl's deleted read, which printed `result->deleted` with no `$`.

**Part 2: thirteen languages.** All thirteen one commands pass at the tag, with nothing open and no defect. The open classes were decided by one written rule per changed sentence (mine/decide2.py). The old rule that carries a v33p decision over to a re-paired class was switched off, because it would have carried perl's old defect records forward.

perl's 14 defect classes are re-decided. The root quick start keeps `use lib 'perl/lib';` and the perl lane runs it 7/7 in each of three models. On a copy with that line removed, the lane fails with "Can't locate DemoSDK.pm". No example prints a hash reference any more.

**Part 3: attacks.** Every attack was re-run on a copy of the merged clone (mutations of provider and forms files, then the guard):
- 14 new attacks aimed at the new checks: 14 caught.
- The guard and tools engineers' 37 attacks: 31 caught, after re-aiming 2 at the new swift form. Five fail nowhere: 2 are caught by the tools, 1 needs an OCaml compiler that is not here, 1 only a reviewer can find, and 1 is no longer a real attack because decision 3 made 'record' a working value for perl. The 37th, G5, is meant to pass.
- The last freeze's 108 mutations: 97 caught, the same 5 not caught as before.

**Checks at the tag:** suite 2631 tests with 0 failures; golden 2/2; all seven lanes pass; the seven unported languages are byte-identical to v32-frozen's output; the tools' self-test runs 235 controls with 0 failed and 2 moved, after re-aiming 16 controls whose text the freeze had re-wrapped.

**Against H1:** breaking interface changes since the first four languages now stand at about 25 to 27, well over H1's limit of about 10. Of the 3 breaking changes in this round, 2 or 3 came from newly ported languages (swift's unwrap, the stream signal, and the utility copy if counted). That refutes H1 on that criterion.

disagreements.runtime_shows: c Entity.fragment.c `return voxgig_clone(self->mtch);` (line 260); clojure Entity.fragment.clj `(vs/clone (deref (:_match ent)))` (line 30); zig Entity.fragment.zig `return h.clone(self.mtch);` (line 315). The match is plain data, so the clone is a real copy.

disagreements.provider_says: copy:true on c go lua perl py rb rust swift zig; ts declared nothing
disagreements.guard_reads: No citation in any language. The guard engineer's note said ts should declare false or omit it, with a pinned reason, and that a clone call must not be cited as proof.
disagreements.survey_says: Q2: go, c, py, rb, php, perl, lua, swift, zig and rust return a new Utility (a shallow copy); ts, js and elixir return the live object.
disagreements.runtime_shows: I opened each copy function and every one allocates a new object. c utility.c:20-21 `Utility* u = (Utility*)calloc(1, sizeof(Utility));`. go utility_type.go:50-51 `u := &Utility{}`. lua utility_type.lua:53-54 `local u = Utility.new()`. perl utility_type.pm:22-24 `my $u = $class->new;`. py utility_type.py:52-53 `u = cls()`. rb utility_type.rb:25-26 `u = ProjectNameUtility.new`. rust utility_type.rs:31 `Rc::new(Utility {`. swift Utility.swift:50-51 `let u = Utility(noregister: true)`. zig utility.zig:71-72 `const u = h.A().create(Utility) ...`. ts Main.fragment.ts:110 `return this._utility.struct.clone(this._utility)`, where clone keeps class instances by reference (StructUtility.ts: `'Object' !== v.constructor.name &&` -> `refs.push(v)`). I ran it in node on the vendored js StructUtility: `clone(classInstance) === instance` is true, and a plain object clones to a new object.
disagreements.decided: All three readings agree. Each of the nine is cited with two quotes: the getter, and the copy function's allocation line. ts now declares `copy: false`, cited to the clone call plus StructUtility's instance rule and `class Utility {`.

disagreements.provider_says: a read template: ts '{var}.deleted()', go '{var}.Deleted()', c '{var}->vt->deleted({var})', zig '{var}.deleted', ocaml '{var}.e_deleted', and so on
disagreements.guard_reads: The guard expected a bare member name and took the first identifier, `var`; its declaration finder could not see a C function-pointer member or a zig struct field.
disagreements.survey_says: Q6: the readers named the same members: c `e->vt->deleted(e)`, zig a public `deleted: bool` field plus `is_deleted()`, ocaml the field `e_deleted`, swift `deleted()` on EntityBase.
disagreements.runtime_shows: c sdk.h `bool (*deleted)(Entity*);`; zig Entity.fragment.zig:47 `deleted: bool = false,`; go Entity.fragment.go `Deleted()`; and the others as the shared engineer listed.
disagreements.decided: The provider is right; I fixed the guard (93060a64). The member is now the last identifier after the {var} slots are stripped, and a field or function-pointer declaration counts (fieldInRuntime). Separately, perl's template `{var}->deleted` printed `result->deleted` with no sigil. Neither the guard nor the survey sees that: I found it reading the page, and fixed it to `${var}->deleted` (120a3c0c).

disagreements.provider_says: facts.record '{var}.data()' and facts.unwrap 'asNative as? Entity', kept separate

Two controls are now caught: the printer dropping the cast (K-swift-record-unwrap-dropped, G8-swift-cast-dropped-adapted) and a record that names `asEntity` (G8-swift-asEntity-adapted).
